small_guidance:
- The conv_transpose (replaced by conv2d) dominates runtime now; the fused pool/htanh/mean/tanh kernel is tiny. Focus tuning on reducing conv time: try `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True` and ensure inputs are `channels_last` (memory_format) for the conv2d call — Ada gets large gains from NHWC fp32 convs.
- For the fused tail kernel, bump `BLOCK_SIZE` to 32768 with `num_warps=8` to halve the loop trips over the 16384-element pooled map; also pass `htanh_min/max` as `tl.constexpr` to bake them into PTX.
- Consider 2D tiling (program per (N, C_tile)) processing multiple channels per program so the per-program reduction amortizes the launch and final tanh; current grid is N*C = 8192 which is fine but per-program work is small.
large_guidance:
- Write a custom Triton conv2d (im2col-style GEMM, one program per (N, OC_tile, HW_tile), channels_last layout) fused with bias add, then pipe directly into max-pool 2x2 + hardtanh + spatial-mean + tanh in a single epilogue — avoid materializing the [N,64,256,256] intermediate. Even partial fusion (conv→pool→htanh writing the pooled tensor) cuts the dominant memory traffic in half.
- Alternatively, implement a true ConvTranspose2d scatter-add kernel for stride=1 case fused with the downstream pool/htanh/mean/tanh — eliminates the weight transpose+flip+contiguous overhead on every forward.
- Persistent kernel design: one program per (N, OC) accumulating the full output spatial reduction in registers/shared memory, streaming conv outputs through pool+htanh without ever writing the 64MB activation. The mean reduction then needs no second kernel.
